questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Italy and I had heard a lot about studying in Bologna since it is a very well-recognized study city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 9.5-10. The overall experience was sooo good, but of course some things could have been better.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. I can't remember it that well. I think the best advice is to not stress too much about all the stuff beforehand, cause it is really chaotic and everything will work out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am not sure. The university did send out a lot of information beforehand and they were actually very quick to reply on e-mail about questions (a lot faster than KU).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you don't discover Leopardi Consulting (or get the number on one of their employees Laif) it is really difficult. They administrate almost all rentals in Bologna, so almost everyone rent through them. When you are in contact with Laif it is really easy and you are sure not to be scammed, but it is also a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Contact Laif/Leopardi Consulting.

I lived in a students' apartment with people from other countries. I can really recommend this. I think it gives you a much more insightful and authentic experience and Bologna is so small that you will definetely meet and get Danish friends as well. I lived with the nicest people from both Europe, Asia and Africa, and I really think it gave me some special friendships and taught me a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is not very good compared to other cities, but it is fine.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't really remember, but I am sure that it was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online meetings and e-mail. If you are in doubt of anything then book an online meeting, it really helps.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted (that was created). It is a bit stupid, cause when you apply for your learning agreement, you will probably have chosen classes that end up not get created, and then you will have to pick new ones from the list of classes that actually did get created.

This is very chaotic and confusing, but it is not necessary to stress about, cause the law classes are really big and the learning agreement will get in place eventually.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask about pre-approval for A LOT of courses, cause you don't know which courses will be created, be overlapping or have a very late exam or bad exam form, so it's nice to be able to choose between a lot of courses (otherwise you will have more waiting time with your learning agremeent, if you need to wait for another pre-approval as well).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the teaching was soooo bad. I was actually really disappointed. Both the teaching and the facilities were very bad (for example the bathrooms, the temperature in the class room, the chairs and tables etc.) (well at least in my building).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was low compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was SO bad in Bologna. A professor would just be talking about random stuff for two hours straight with no break and no powerpoint or other supporting material, so it was very difficult to actually follow what was going on in class.

I think people from other countries are more used to this, cause they were really engaging in class and took notes to everything (literally everything) the professors said.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative constitutionalism, Gender and the law, Fundamental Rights and EU law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The texts in comparative constitutionalism were very interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really know, but I think a lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get the ESN card (gives you discount on beer and ryanair tickets) and follow ESN Bologna on Instagram and attend some of their activities. It is a nice way to do some things that you normally don't do in Denmark. The free walking-tour was very nice, and every tuesday is pub night at the Irish Pub on via Zamboni, so the street is completely full (when the weather is ok).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: More of Italy! Modena, Ferrara (very cute), Parma, Firenze, Rome, more of South Italy (especially Naples and Matera!!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend as much stuff as possible (this means irish every tuesday). The city is full of students and people really want to chat, so it should be easy. Have aperol at Freuds, it is always full of students as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the nice people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do it! Studying in Bologna is sooo amazing. You won't regret it (even though the teaching is very bad, but all the good things will out weight this!)

And book a room in an international apartment and not just with other Danes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live in Italy in such a beautiful city and to meet so many new amazing people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not that many

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
